html:
Emomali Rahmon has led Tajikistan since 1992, first as head of parliament and from 1994 as president. He was born in 1952 in Dangara, in the south, and ran a collective farm before the civil war lifted him to power.

He ended the war with the peace deal of 1997, then built one of the most closed governments in the region. Rivals were jailed or killed, his relatives took top posts, and in 2015 he was given the title Leader of the Nation, with lifelong immunity. He dropped the Russian ending of his name, Rakhmonov, in 2007.

He made the Samanid emir Ismail Samani the national hero and pushed the giant Rogun Dam. Most families depend on money sent home by men working in Russia, which makes Tajikistan one of the most remittance-dependent countries on earth.
